executed_plan.hypothesis: Injecting 2 s latency will increase observer data_age to ~2.5 s, keep error_rate <5 %, and delay generation of speed‑related alerts by roughly the added latency, observable as a ~2 s lag between telemetry receipt and alert appearance.
executed_plan.reason: 2 s is below the 30 s client timeout but above the 1 s update interval, allowing us to see if alert evaluation is delayed without triggering aborts.

notes: data_age_s = now - client event time of the state the app shows. server_age_s = now - the app's own last_telemetry_at. latency_ms = observer read latency (direct, not proxied); writes.latency_ms = loadgen round trip through the proxy.

experiments.hypothesis: Injecting 2 s latency will increase observer data_age to ~2.5 s, keep error_rate <5 %, and delay generation of speed‑related alerts by roughly the added latency, observable as a ~2 s lag between telemetry receipt and alert appearance.
experiments.reason: 2 s is below the 30 s client timeout but above the 1 s update interval, allowing us to see if alert evaluation is delayed without triggering aborts.

experiments.hypothesis: Injecting 6 s latency will push data_age mean above 5 s while the app still has no offline detection; we expect no device_offline alerts but a hidden_delay (data_age – server_age) of ~5 s, confirming that the alert engine uses server_age not client‑visible age.
experiments.reason: 6 s latency (new value between prior 5 k and 8 k runs) tests the hidden_delay hypothesis without exceeding abort limits.

analysis.injected: 2000 ms latency injected on loadgen->fleet-api for 30.7 s
analysis.hypothesis_reason: data_age_s increased to ~2.0 s (close to the expected ~2.5 s) and error_rate remained 0.0 % (<5 %), but no speed‑related alerts were generated, so the expected alert‑delay effect could not be verified
analysis.weakness: data_age_s mean rose to 2.043 s while server_age_s mean was only 0.388 s, yielding a hidden_delay_s of 1.655 s; because the app does not store client timestamps it cannot see the true staleness of telemetry, resulting in potentially stale data being presented without any alert

recommended_fix.change: Store the client‑provided telemetry timestamp and use it when calculating data_age so the app can detect stale data
